title: Health and Household
summary: Illness, body, home tasks, requests, and rules at home.
whyItMatters: Health and household language helps you describe a basic symptom, identify what needs attention at home, and coordinate simple care or chores. These situations require clear nouns, practical verbs, and short statements about problems and needs.

mentalModel.title: Name the place, problem, and action
mentalModel.content: For health, identify the body part and symptom; for the home, identify the room or object and the task.

mentalModel.title: Separate state from action
mentalModel.content: Use 'sein' or 'haben' for a condition and an action verb for the response: 'Ich habe Kopfschmerzen. Ich nehme eine Tablette.'

mentalModel.title: Connect responsibility to routine
mentalModel.content: Household tasks become usable when attached to a person and time: 'Heute räumt Alex die Küche auf.'

ruleBlocks.title: Describe common symptoms
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Ich habe ...' for Schmerzen, Fieber, Husten, and Schnupfen; use 'Mir ist ...' in common chunks such as 'Mir ist schlecht'.

ruleBlocks.title: Name the affected body part
ruleBlocks.content: Use clear statements such as 'Mein Rücken tut weh' and 'Ich habe Schmerzen im Bein'.

ruleBlocks.title: Learn chores as verb-object chunks
ruleBlocks.content: Practice das Geschirr spülen, den Müll rausbringen, das Bad putzen, and das Zimmer aufräumen.

ruleBlocks.title: State simple household expectations
ruleBlocks.content: Use modal or imperative chunks: 'Bitte mach das Fenster zu' and 'Wir müssen heute putzen'.

sentenceStructure: Separable household verbs split in main clauses.
A direct object identifies what receives the household action.
Use short sequential sentences for a problem and response.

concepts: name common chores and home rules
explain medical history and detailed symptoms

comparisons.summary: The pronoun lesson replaces known people or objects in health and household actions: 'Ich nehme sie' or 'Ruf ihn an'.
The communication lesson turns problems and chores into requests, instructions, and advice.

examples.de: Ich habe Kopfschmerzen und brauche Ruhe.
examples.en: I have a headache and need rest.

examples.de: Mein Rücken tut seit heute Morgen weh.
examples.en: My back has hurt since this morning.

examples.de: Nimm die Tablette nach dem Essen.
Ich spüle das Geschirr, und du bringst den Müll raus.
examples.en: I wash the dishes, and you take out the rubbish.

examples.de: Bitte räum dein Zimmer vor dem Abendessen auf.
examples.en: Please tidy your room before dinner.

commonMistakes.reason: German uses 'haben' with this symptom noun.
The prefix of a separable verb moves to the end in a main clause.
The masculine direct object uses accusative 'den'.

specialCases: 'Mir ist schlecht' uses a dative person and describes nausea or feeling unwell.
'Wehtun' agrees with the painful body part: 'Der Rücken tut weh', 'Die Beine tun weh'.
Medical emergencies require direct professional help beyond this lesson's routine language.
tips: Pair every symptom with one sensible response.
Assign real household tasks on a weekly chart.
Practice separable verbs with a visual gap between verb and prefix.
